inputs.issue_title: Add rate limiting to GitHub API client
inputs.issue_body: We're hitting GitHub's rate limit (5000 req/hour). Add rate limiting to the client so we stay under the limit.
inputs.research_context: GitHub API returns X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers. Secondary rate limits exist for abuse detection (no explicit header). Conditional requests (If-None-Match/304) don't count against the limit.
inputs.gathered_context: github/client.go wraps net/http. Used by dispatcher (polling), committer (PR creation), and reviewer (comment posting). Polling runs every 30s across multiple repos.
inputs.conventions: Zero external dependencies. Use context.Context for cancellation. Shared state must be goroutine-safe.

assertions.value:
This is a HARD planning task. Check the plan against these criteria:
1. Identifies that rate limiting must be goroutine-safe because multiple callers (dispatcher, committer, reviewer) share the client concurrently
2. Proposes reading rate limit headers from GitHub API responses (X-RateLimit-Remaining or X-RateLimit-Reset) rather than using a fixed-rate timer
3. Addresses what happens when the limit is hit: the plan must include a wait/backoff strategy, not just an error return
4. Does NOT propose adding external rate-limiting libraries (e.g., golang.org/x/time/rate) — must use stdlib only
5. Mentions or accounts for the fact that multiple repos share a single rate limit budget
